landing.title: Find the career that actually fits you
landing.subtitle: Masar analyses your school grades, SAT and IELTS scores, interests and personality, and returns 10 ranked careers in the UAE job market — each with a plain explanation of why, the skills you still need, and a learning plan to get there.
landing.demoNote: 5 answers is not an assessment. The full one takes 15 minutes and uses your grades and personality too.
landing.step1Body: Emirate, school, grade level and your MOE track: General, Advanced or Elite.
landing.step2Body: 6 core subjects, plus SAT and IELTS scores if you have them. Both are optional.
landing.step3Body: 10 Holland RIASEC interest items and 10 Big Five personality items.
landing.step4Body: Ranked careers, a skill-gap chart, a 4-phase learning roadmap and a PDF report.
landing.f1Body: Every match tells you which of your grades, interests or traits produced it. No black box.
landing.f2Body: See your estimated level against what each career actually requires, skill by skill.
landing.f3Body: Specific courses from 120 options — free and paid, Arabic and English, global and UAE providers.
landing.f4Body: Ask about any career, salary, university pathway or skill, in English or Arabic, at any hour.
landing.f5Body: MOE tracks, EmSAT and SAT, UAE universities, AED salary ranges and the national strategies each career serves.
landing.f6Body: Download your full profile and plan as a bilingual PDF for your parents or your counsellor.
landing.sectorsSubtitle: Every career in Masar maps onto a sector the UAE is actively building.
landing.ctaFinalBody: No cost, no commitment. You can stop after any step and come back later.
landing.demoTitle: 2 questions in, you will know more than you did
landing.demoSubtitle: Both surveys run the real model — the same one behind the full assessment — and draw fresh questions every time, so you can run either one twice and learn something new.
landing.demoQuickBlurb: 5 questions, drawn at random, about the kind of work you want to still be doing in 10 years.
landing.demoDeepBlurb: 10 different questions on majors, risk and what you would keep if a machine took the rest.
landing.demoNoteDeep: 10 answers still is not an assessment — but it is close enough to be worth arguing with. The full one adds your grades and test scores.

about.title: About Masar AI
about.methodIntro: Masar combines 2 models rather than relying on one, because neither answers the whole question on its own.
about.m1Body: A Random Forest trained on 5,000 generated student profiles predicts which of the 15 sectors fits a student. Logistic Regression and K-Nearest Neighbours were trained as baselines for comparison.
about.m2Body: Each career has an ideal profile vector. We compare the student's 20-dimensional profile against it with a mean-centred cosine similarity, which ranks individual careers inside and across sectors.
about.m3Body: The final score is 45% classifier, 45% similarity and 10% labour-market demand. Demand is capped deliberately: a guidance system that chases fashion would recreate the problem it exists to solve.
about.m4Body: For each match we surface the 3 profile dimensions that contributed most, and only where the student and the career are both strong — a shared strength, never a shared absence.
about.dataBody: No public dataset links UAE school grades, RIASEC interests and Big Five traits to career outcomes. Rather than claim one, Masar ships a deterministic synthetic dataset generator with a documented causal story, and states its limits openly. High accuracy on this data demonstrates that the pipeline works — not that the recommendations are externally validated.

model.title: About the model
model.subtitle: What the recommender is, how it was measured, and where it is weak.
model.syntheticNote: No real labelled dataset of UAE students and their careers exists, so the model is trained on a synthetic cohort generated from the ideal profiles in the career catalog. It therefore learns the relationships we encoded, and cannot discover a relationship we did not. Accuracy figures describe performance on that synthetic distribution, not on real students. This is a demonstration of method, not a validated instrument.
model.proseNote: Long-form career descriptions are generated from each career's structured fields rather than written individually.
model.parityNote: Recommendations are computed in your browser. A parity test asserts the browser implementation matches the Python model to within 1e-6 on 50 fixed profiles.

scholarships.title: Scholarships and funding
scholarships.subtitle: Every route to paying for university in the UAE that this catalog holds — government scholarships, university awards, employer sponsorship and the money almost nobody applies for.
scholarships.matchBody: Matched against your emirate, your track and your recommended majors.
scholarships.matchNoProfile: Complete the assessment and this page will sort itself around your results.
scholarships.howToTitle: 3 things students get wrong about this
scholarships.howTo1Title: Apply before you are sure you qualify
scholarships.howTo1Body: Need-based funds are the least applied-for money in the system, because students assume they will not qualify and never ask. The cost of asking is an email.
scholarships.howTo2Title: A bond is a decision, not a discount
scholarships.howTo2Body: Employer sponsorship pays for everything and commits years of your life to one organisation. That can be an excellent trade — but make it knowingly, and read the length.
scholarships.howTo3Body: Master's and PhD places are routinely paid for by the department through assistantships. Ask the academic, not the scholarships office.
scholarships.indicativeWarning: Every record here is indicative. Terms and deadlines change every intake — confirm on the provider's own page before planning around it.
